Only a grammar-accepted complete verified-absent branch may resume solely at the no-Docker failed-task CAS.
recovery_prefix_grammar.ownership_authority: a pre-create interruption with no durable ID may run only the three non-destructive pair-label container/volume/network discovery lists; all-zero proves absence, while any match requires manual handling and authorizes no delete. Destructive cleanup requires all three complete initial setup zero-proof list receipts plus either the durable created ID or the exact one-container sequence-1 discovery result matching both unguessable labels. A second container match, missing prior zero proof, control identity drift, or journal ambiguity performs no deletion and returns archive_run_recovery_evidence_incomplete. recovery_prefix_grammar.crash_matrix_requirement: Gate A parameterizes every setup command, every operation/inspection/ordinary-success cleanup command, the pending-to-interrupted journal transition, the pre-create/no-ID discovery path, every command in each 3/4/5 recovery cleanup branch, and the complete-cleanup-to-task-CAS boundary at prepared, result_recorded, each artifact-prefix, receipt-complete, journal-complete, and task-CAS boundaries; only grammar-accepted prefixes with no cleanup started may start cleanup, a complete verified-absent branch may finish only task CAS without Docker, and any other crash during ordinary-success or recovery cleanup fails closed without another Docker command
recovery_prefix_grammar.pending_command_types: pending_command command_class is setup|operation|inspection|cleanup; sequence is the class-local bounded positive integer; operation is the closed identifier; argv/environment/control identities and all result digests are 64 lowercase hex; stage is prepared|result_recorded; prepared requires exit/stream fields null and artifact_prefix_count 0; result_recorded requires integer exit, exact stream values, and artifact_prefix_count 0..4 or 0..5 only for inspection. interrupted_command is null in normal/success journals or an immutable exact copy of the sole normal pending_command moved by the recovery-start journal successor; it is never itself active or cleared.
recovery_prefix_grammar.completed_sequence_rules: setup/operation/inspection lists are duplicate-free contiguous prefixes starting at 1 with maxima 9/12/24. Ordinary-success cleanup is exactly 1..4. Recovery cleanup is the exact contiguous prefix of its selected 3-, 4-, or 5-command branch. A grammar-accepted complete branch plus cleanup_status verified_absent and empty final resource lists may await only task CAS; an exact accepted prefix whose last command has a fully durable nonzero result/artifact group, or an exact final zero-exit branch with a non-empty owned-resource list, and cleanup_status failed is archive_cleanup_failed; every other nonempty prefix observed on re-entry is evidence-incomplete. Receipt paths/digests must exist completely, and pending_command is exactly the next class-local sequence.
recovery_prefix_grammar.journal_integrity: strict I-JSON with exact fields and no self-authentication claim; before a success summary its authority comes from exclusive lease, durable ordered publication, task/binding equality, and closed artifact-prefix validation; corruption or ambiguity fails without deletion; the final summary later binds its exact bytes externally
recovery_prefix_grammar.recovery_cleanup_branches: cleanup execution may start once and only while completed_cleanup_sequences is empty and no ordinary-success or prior recovery cleanup command has been prepared. With a durable created_container_id, cleanup is exactly four commands: docker-rm, pair-labeled container-list, volume-list, network-list. Without a durable ID and before container-create could have run, cleanup is exactly three non-destructive pair-label discovery lists for container, volume, and network; all must be empty and any match fails without deletion. Without a durable ID after create may have succeeded, sequence 1 is the fixed pair-label container discovery: zero matches selects the three-command discovery, volume-list, network-list branch; exactly one dual-label match selects the five-command discovery, docker-rm, container-list, volume-list, network-list branch only when all three initial setup zero proofs are complete. A second match, missing zero proof, or malformed discovery aborts before deletion and is evidence-incomplete. Any command failure closes cleanup_status failed immediately with no later command. Any non-empty final owned-resource result also closes failed without deleting that remaining resource. All groups use receipts/cleanup/{sequence}-{operation}; no recovery-discovery directory or unjournaled command exists. After an exact complete verified-absent branch, re-entry is allowed only to finish task CAS and issues no Docker command.
recovery_prefix_grammar.cleanup_status_transition: cleanup_status starts null. Every fully durable cleanup command result/artifact group is appended and its pending_command cleared in one atomic successor. A zero-exit non-final command leaves phase cleanup and cleanup_status null. If the current command exits nonzero, that same successor sets phase cleanup_verified and cleanup_status failed and closes the selected branch. If the exact final branch command exits zero and all final resource lists are empty, that same successor sets phase cleanup_verified and cleanup_status verified_absent; if an owned-resource list is non-empty, it instead sets cleanup_status failed. Phase cleanup_verified means terminal cleanup evidence was evaluated; cleanup_status distinguishes absence from failure. There is no accepted terminal receipt/status-null gap. A prepared-only, result-only, partial, or uncertain command cannot set a non-null status. Once non-null, cleanup_status is immutable.
recovery_prefix_grammar.complete_cleanup_equivalence: for a still-running revision-2/3 task, an exact complete ordinary-success four-command cleanup and an exact complete recovery cleanup are intentionally the same classification equivalence class: both may only finish the failed-task CAS with zero Docker. Origin is therefore not an authorization discriminator; the exact accepted command/receipt prefix and final absence proofs are.
